Forwarding OptimumRetail alert — they report p95 jump and 5xxs after our v2.1b-tight-quant rollout. Initial triage notes:

- v2.1b-tight-quant: new 4-bit quantization with more aggressive kernel path (deque pooling enabled). Deployed 07:15–07:30 UTC into dedicated pool OR-3.
- Retrofit tests in staging showed negligible latency change, but those workloads didn’t hit long-sequence hotpaths.

Asks:
1) Marcus: can you confirm kernel selection logs and whether fallback paths triggered?
2) Monica: does the autoscaler/instance health show CPU or NVMe pressure?
3) Jonas: can you run a quick trace for KV cache eviction and prefix cache hit rate?

I’ll loop back to OptimumRetail with the first-hour plan. We should treat as P1 and pull exec attention if we can’t stabilize in 90m.

--
Irene Choi
Customer Reliability Manager, Redwood Inference

From: marcus.lin@redwood.com
To: irene.choi@redwood.com, monica.patel@redwood.com, jonas.weber@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-09T08:46:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Sudden p95 jump & 5xxs after today's model push

Quick findings from the OR-3 pool (07:10–08:40 window):
- Kernel selection: aggressive fused-kernel path chosen for 4-bit dequant (we saw a fallback attempt at 07:52 for ~3% of requests due to transient OOMs).
- GPU mem pressure: average +22% compared to baseline; peaks correspond with long-sequence (>=768 tokens) requests.
- KV cache churn: eviction rate up 6x; prefix cache hit dropped from 88% -> 51% on high-load hosts.

Hypothesis: tighter quant increases per-request temporary memory and changes allocation pattern such that KV/prefix cache eviction rises for long sequences, causing extra recompute and timeouts. Also observed elevated CUDA kernel queue latency for fused kernels under high concurrency.

Immediate mitigation options:
- Roll forward to v2.0-stable (previous quant profile) — fastest rollback.
- Force kernel fallback to safer dequant path for v2.1b for OR-3 (config flag) — medium risk but preserves model variant.
- Temporary route heavy-sequence traffic to dedicated fallback region (OR-2) with looser quantization.

I recommend rollback to v2.0-stable while we collect full traces. I’ll upload perf snapshot and kernel logs to the drive.

--
Marcus Lin
Principal SRE, Redwood Inference

Summary of current status (final in-thread update):

- 2026-10-09 09:18 UTC: OR-3 rollback to v2.0-stable completed; p95 and 5xxs returned to baseline within ~7 minutes.
- Root cause (interim): tight-quant (v2.1b) introduced allocation patterns that increased KV/prefix cache churn and triggered a small subset of fused kernels to enqueue under high concurrency, increasing latency and transient OOMs for long-sequence requests.
- Immediate remediation: rollback + routing changes; we disabled fused-kernel path for the v2.1b rollout internally and added long-sequence synthetic scenarios to the preflight test matrix.

Requests and exec asks:
1) OptimumRetail: Redwood will provide an executive summary (1 page) and the proposed goodwill credit (2 days of service credit) for business impact; please confirm if that aligns with your procurement expectations.
2) Redwood Leadership: I’m recommending a temporary hold on aggressive tight-quant releases for any customer with long-sequence hotpaths until we finish a 2-week validation plan. Requesting product + model ops signoff.
3) Ops: full post-mortem (including kernel traces and memory profiles) due EOD 10/14.

Attachments: heapdump-20261011.bin (capture), MA_plan_v2.xlsx (updated). Drive: https://redwood-drive.company/optimumretail/triage-notes-1011
